name: Inverted totalitarianism
summary: Inverted totalitarianism is Sheldon Wolin's term for a form of total power in which corporate and state power fuse in a nominally democratic country. Elections persist but are managed, media and money shape opinion, welfare and labor are weakened, citizens are kept apathetic, and a permanent-war Superpower pursues global reach. Wolin argues this reverses classical totalitarianism, which was state-led, ideological and mobilizing.
scope: Wolin's thesis as set out in his 2003 Nation essay and the 2008 book Democracy Incorporated, as described by reference works and reviews. It is a critical diagnosis held by a democratic-left audience, not a governing program, so many statements are inferred; it excludes the later extensions by other writers.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Wolin condemns the cutback of New Deal programs including public health as a "selective abdication" of government responsibility for citizens' well-being, so adherents favor state guarantees.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of insecurity-by-design for workers and the goal of corporate strategies to weaken labor; he does not discuss the minimum wage itself.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The thesis is that unchecked economic power dominates politics and hollows out democracy; adherents reject the claim that markets serve the public better than democratic government.

public-ownership.rationale: Wolin attacks privatization of public functions but his remedies stress democratic participation and regulation, not nationalization, so the answer is split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to concentrated corporate wealth buying politics; he does not give a tax program.

unions-good.rationale: He says the destruction of the remnants of trade unions remains a corporate goal and treats collective bargaining as a democratic gain won against elites.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: property rights of corporations are what he sees as trumping democratic control, so an adherent would not treat them as nearly inviolable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His remedies call for rolling back managed democracy and strengthening regulation; the whole thesis is that corporate power escaped state control.

cut-welfare.rationale: He describes the cutting of Social Security, welfare and public housing as a deliberate strategy of managed democracy that produces insecurity.

worker-ownership.rationale: He is hostile to corporate rule but offers no worker-ownership program; adherents are split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Surveillance is not a central theme; inferred from his critique of post-9/11 executive power and a managed public, and from democratic-liberal concern for civil liberties.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by Wolin, and no principle in the thesis settles it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' concern with corporate-filtered speech does not settle the question of legal speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: He holds that inverted totalitarianism needs no charismatic leader and that managerial executive power erodes constitutional restraint; a leader bypassing gridlock is the opposite of his democratic ideal.

state-harmful.rationale: Wolin wants democratic citizens to retake and exercise power over state and economy; he is not an anarchist.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in his work; adherents are not tied to a view.

empower-police-military.rationale: He criticizes the military-industrial complex as sitting outside government with huge budgets and wants empire and militarism rolled back.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources read never take up sex work law, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

decide-locally.rationale: The publisher summary says democracy's best hope lies in citizens learning to exercise power at the local level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; he contrasts the classical regimes' punishment with an economy of fear but takes no stand on penal policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: he treats culture-war family issues as manufactured divisions that obscure class differences, not as foundations to defend.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He treats gay marriage mainly as a wedge issue designed to divide the public, and does not state a position on it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed beyond treating moral controversies as managed divisions.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of religion deployed as a wedge and of religious charities within state-funded programs.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed directly; adherents' egalitarianism suggests sympathy but he does not state a program.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources read never take up the nature of gender, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred: his target is nationalist-imperial Superpower and he stresses that inverted totalitarianism is not nationalist but global, so cultural preservation is no concern of his.

gradual-change.rationale: He wants radical democratic revival and sees established institutions as already captured, though he also favors patient local work.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The sources read never take up immigration levels, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; he opposes unilateral US hegemony but does not advocate supranational power.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: he attacks global corporate power and neoliberal outsourcing as tools that make workers insecure.

nation-first.rationale: He opposes US superpower hegemony and preemptive war, but does not defend cooperation as a principle, so the answer is mildly negative.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He condemns preemptive war and the Iraq invasion as imperial; humanitarian intervention is not discussed.

open-borders.rationale: The sources read never take up border policy, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

limit-growth.rationale: The book criticizes the quest for an ever-expanding economy, but gives no environmental program.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His reform list includes environmental protections and regulation; drastic action is inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He says technology and social science are used to manage opinion and elections, so he is skeptical of technology as a solution.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The sources read never take up nuclear power, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

revolution-justified.rationale: He urges democratic renewal through citizens exercising power and checks and balances, not revolution, though he does not rule it out.

experts-over-public.rationale: The book has a chapter on intellectual elites against democracy and objects to managerial technocratic rule of a shepherded public.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: he opposes both classical totalitarian state control and corporate control, and favors democratic power.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split on market forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: The sources read never take up land taxation, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from opposition to concentrated wealth; not stated.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; he defends public welfare institutions but has no stated view on this design.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; he attacks outsourcing but not on trade-policy terms.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He sees state-corporate fusion as the danger, so state steering of investment toward strategic industries sits uneasily with his view.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources read never take up the distribution of small property, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He is a democrat reformer, not an advocate of abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; as a critic of unregulated private economic power he would not hand money wholly to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: state-recognized bodies of employers and workers resemble the classical fascist model he sets inverted totalitarianism against, and he stresses participatory democracy.

one-party-rule.rationale: He argues against totalitarian one-party ideological rule and for democratic participation, even as he thinks two parties are both captured by corporate power.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from his democratic commitments; the topic is not addressed.

democracy-best.rationale: His whole project defends democracy as the legitimate political form against managed democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from his preference for citizens exercising power directly at local level, though he does not specify referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: He favors participatory local democracy but does not endorse councils replacing parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources read never take up regional secession, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

natural-rulers.rationale: He argues the framers distrusted the demos and built elite protections, and treats democratic rule by ordinary citizens as the ideal.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; he rejects coercive state terror but is silent on resistance.

war-builds-character.rationale: He regards permanent mobilization and war as the engine of Superpower and as incompatible with democracy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of religious charities in state-funded programs and of religion used for wedge politics.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred as above; not stated directly.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He opposes privatization of public functions, which he sees as the steady rise of corporate power as governing partner.

military-superiority.rationale: He opposes US global hegemony, the huge defense budget and preemptive war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He describes inverted totalitarianism as non-racial and non-nationalist, and nothing suggests he favors ethnic nationhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He traces a long struggle between elites and the demos from Greece onward, but not Marx's class-conflict thesis as such.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He stresses class differences being obscured but gives no stated view on equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources read never take up Indigenous land rights, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources read never take up colonial reparations, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to imperial hegemony and unifying ideologies.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He decries politics reduced to factional self-interest and wants a commitment to the common good, but he does not take a moral stand on self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from his defense of civil liberties against a managed state; he also stresses civic participation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources read never take up the intrinsic value of nature, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

limit-population.rationale: The sources read never take up population policy, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He criticizes endless growth but does not call industrial civilization a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He sees technology as a tool of management and manipulation, so he would not push disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources read never take up human enhancement, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from his objection to managerial, expert-run and technique-driven politics replacing democratic deliberation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources read never take up encryption, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

restore-past-order.rationale: He looks back to democratic moments, but does not seek restoration of a lost order over progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He criticizes cost-effectiveness and managerial profit logic as replacing commitment to the common good.

direct-action.rationale: He prizes citizens exercising power, but also wants to restore working democratic institutions; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of his thesis; he is a democratic reformer.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not stated; he defends welfare but has no theory of distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: The sources read never take up production for use versus profit, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He blames profit-driven corporate dominance but does not use a labor theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He argues against totalitarian rule and for democratic power, so a dictatorship of any class is outside his view.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; mildly negative as inferred from his opposition to state-directed totalism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He links economic expansion, Superpower and permanent war but does not claim inevitability.

taxation-theft.rationale: He wants public institutions and welfare funded and defended, the opposite of this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources read never take up the limits of state interference in private conduct, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He defends collective gains such as union rights and democratic power, not an individualist-only account.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to militarization and empire.

exit-over-voice.rationale: He argues citizens must exercise voice and power; exit as a substitute would be an abdication.

state-as-business.rationale: He criticizes managerial, cost-effectiveness and business logic in government as a core feature of managed democracy.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from his view that insecurity and cutbacks leave citizens powerless, so material conditions affect real participation.

media-academia-power.rationale: He says power sits with corporations and the military, with corporate media and co-opted universities serving them, not exceeding elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred; the thesis rejects racialist ideology as driver of the system, and egalitarian democracy.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: corporatist representation is the fascist form he contrasts with managed democracy.

total-state.rationale: Classical totalitarianism, with a state directing everything, is exactly what he contrasts and warns against, even while calling the inverted form totalistic.

national-rebirth.rationale: He treats nationalist mobilization myths as features of classical totalitarianism that inverted totalitarianism lacks and opposes.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He condemns empire, Lebensraum-style preemptive war and global hegemony.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He says elites and media shape images and opinion but does not take an epistemological stance.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources read never take up universal moral truths, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

single-common-good.rationale: The Wikipedia summary names the missing commitment to finding where the common good lies as a central failing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources read never take up diaspora return rights, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

revive-national-language.rationale: The sources read never take up language revival, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from his demand to extend democratic power to citizens and against corporate rule, though he does not state a workplace vote.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to privatization of public functions.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from opposition to austerity-style cutbacks of public provision.

economic-freedom.rationale: His thesis is that unbridled economic power undermines political freedom, the reverse of this claim.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: he prefers constitutional and democratic limits over personal moral leadership.

national-self-determination.rationale: The sources read never take up national self-determination, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

force-without-un.rationale: He condemns preemptive war and unilateral use of force by Superpower.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources read never take up reason versus faith as a guide, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources read never take up welfare eligibility for immigrants, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from his condemnation of welfare cutbacks and of insecurity as a control tool.

class-collaboration.rationale: He sees corporate power dominating labor and wants unions strengthened, not cooperation on corporate terms.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred; unrelated to his thesis and opposed to his democratic traditionalism.

dominated-front.rationale: The sources read never take up a common front of dominated countries, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

workers-nation.rationale: The sources read never take up national versus international labor organizing, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred; not part of his program.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation by race is classical-totalitarian-style racial ideology, and he stresses the equal democratic citizen.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He holds that economic power dominates the state and legislators answer to corporate lobbyists, close to this claim though not a Marxist theory.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from his support for environmental protections and criticism of corporate influence.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The sources read never take up immigrant assimilation, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: the claim is a conspiracy theory outside his structural analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from his wish for real alternatives rather than managed two-party elections.

national-mission.rationale: He criticizes the American claim to be the model of democracy worldwide as part of Superpower.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources read never take up structural patriarchy, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He treats corporate capture of legislators as normal and not corruption, but he says political elites serve corporate power rather than the people; agree in substance.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: eugenic policies belong to the classical totalitarian model and conflict with democratic equality.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to militarism and unchecked state power.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He wants a state that protects welfare and checks corporate power.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Democratic equality of the demos is central to his project.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The sources read never take up socialism in one country, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources read never take up settler colonialism, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The sources read never take up a uniform civil code, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The sources read never take up cattle slaughter, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of religion entangled with state-funded programs.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; he opposes enlarged state power under external threat, as with permanent war.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His critique is that elections no longer provide meaningful consent, which presupposes consent as the test of legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: The sources read never take up trade balances, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from democratic principles; this is a classical-totalitarian tool.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed in libertarian terms, though he opposes preemptive war.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred: competition and struggle between peoples is the imperial-Darwinist logic he opposes.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from concern for democratic openness; not addressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Fits his concern with unchecked, unaccountable power, though he does not use the republican term.

separated-powers.rationale: His reform list includes restoring checks and balances, and he treats the unchecked fusion of state and economic power as the danger.

vanguard-party.rationale: He opposes totalitarian parties and wants citizens exercising power themselves.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He defends welfare and public housing and criticizes the exploitation of the poor by the system.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: He defends public housing but the sale of it is not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He says destroying union remnants is a corporate goal, so legal restriction of strikes is part of what he opposes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred from his focus on institutional power as the cause of insecurity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: He traces democratic history from Athens but takes no stated view on lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He criticizes post-9/11 emergency-style executive power and the erosion of constitutional limits.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The sources read never take up price controls on food, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

party-controls-media.rationale: He opposes state control of information, even while arguing private corporate media narrows opinion.

party-commands-army.rationale: Classical totalitarian feature he contrasts against.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The sources read never take up naturalization periods, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The sources read never take up legislators' pay, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of party-managed politics.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The sources read never take up supranational union, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from his concern with executive power eroding constitutional limits.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The sources read never take up church governance, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He opposes imperial war but does not state a defeatist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from democratic and liberal commitments.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from his concern about concentrated and unaccountable executive power.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from his goal of accountable power exercised by citizens.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He wants empire rolled back; alliances as such are not addressed.

people-in-arms.rationale: He opposes militarism and the military-industrial complex; armed citizenry is not addressed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources read never take up rural versus urban life, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources read never take up reunification of divided nations, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: He criticizes intellectual elites and co-opted universities, but his own view is scholarly and not anti-intellectual.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources read never take up cultural hierarchy, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; mildly negative inferred from his concern for state power.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He treats cultural issues as divisions managed to obscure class; no stance.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of religion used to divide and of its entanglement with the state.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources read never take up pornography law, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

minority-language-support.rationale: The sources read never take up minority languages, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The sources read never take up religious exemptions from general laws, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed, though his concern for a depoliticized, uniform public is consonant.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The sources read never take up foreign debt cancellation, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources read never take up postcolonial economic transformation, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He treats the Constitution as framed to protect elite power, but gives no stated view on rewriting it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He opposes sacrificing democracy for growth; his critique is of the pursuit of endless expansion over democratic life.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The sources read never take up foreign aid duties, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from opposition to militarism and superpower.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources read never take up how heads of state are elected, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The sources read never take up central bank independence, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The sources read never take up land-for-peace settlements, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

delink-world-market.rationale: The sources read never take up dependency theory remedies, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources read never take up the labor aristocracy thesis, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian democratic commitments and opposition to unchecked private power.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He treats constitutional restraints as vital for democracy even where the framers designed them for elites.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The sources read never take up colonial-era treaties, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic rule is his central value.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; he is concerned with executive power but also with corporate control of legislatures.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The sources read never take up animal sentience, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The sources read never take up animal use, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He wants power exercised by the demos itself, not elite benevolence.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He says every apathetic citizen is a silent enlistee in inverted totalitarianism.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He says private media, advertising and image management shape perception and breed political apathy.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Managed democracy secures legitimacy through controlled elections and opinion management, not only coercion.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The sources read never take up world-systems theory, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources read never take up citizenship requirements for office, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

party-own-road.rationale: The sources read never take up national roads to socialism, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The sources read never take up development strategy, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to expansionism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources read never take up Indigenous political leadership, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; he is anti-totalitarian but frames the US differently.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He sees inverted totalitarianism as distinct from Nazi and Stalinist forms yet totalistic like them, so no clear stance on equating them.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The sources read never take up contested monuments, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources read never take up boys' and men's disadvantage, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources read never take up domestic violence services, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He rejects the Superpower claim to be the democratic model for the world, but does not defend regional relativism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He wants the military and empire rolled back and treats the military-industrial complex as an unaccountable power.

paid-care-work.rationale: The sources read never take up pay for domestic work, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources read never take up filial duty, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from his criticism of intellectual and expert elites against democracy.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The sources read never take up foreign takeovers of firms, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The sources read never take up divorce law, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from his wish for accountable citizen power.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: He criticizes the dismantling of Social Security and privatization of public functions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The sources read never take up land tenure, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from his emphasis on checks on executive and economic power.

single-official-language.rationale: The sources read never take up official language policy, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The sources read never take up foreign land ownership, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The sources read never take up disparate-impact discrimination law, and the managed-democracy thesis gives no basis for a side.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He says consumerism and an ever-expanding economy help keep citizens passive and depoliticized.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to preemptive war and imperial intervention.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to imperial hegemony and Superpower.

corporate-influence.rationale: Wolin and reviewers describe lobbying, contributions and the revolving door as the normal channel of corporate dominance over government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Wolin does not address it; his concern is domestic corporate power over the state, so adherents have no clear lean.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; the thesis concerns corporate-state power, giving no lean on birth-rate policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed in Wolin's critique of corporate power; no clear lean.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from his critique of weakened welfare and labour protections under corporate power, which favours stronger state provision for workers.

democratic-peace.rationale: He argues the US as a nominal democracy pursues permanent war and global reach, and rejects that democratic form ensures peace; inferred from this.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; Wolin stresses democratic participation and fugitive resistance but offers no stand on a general duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: His critique of the permanent-war Superpower and imperial reach implies opposing intervention abroad; inferred, not a stated principle.

industrial-unions.rationale: He defends labour unions against their decline but does not take a stand on industrial versus craft form; inferred sympathy.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He diagnoses structural corporate-state power, not conspiracy by a minority, and it is a left-democratic critique.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He treats managed democracy and secrecy and media control as central to inverted totalitarianism, so transparency is the remedy.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed beyond his critique of corporate globalisation; no clear lean.

informal-organisation.rationale: He values local democratic participation and episodic 'fugitive democracy' but not explicitly against formal unions; adherents are split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; he criticises US unilateralism but does not argue about law precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: He criticises the fusion of evangelical religion with state power in the US and a democratic-left audience rejects a religiously defined nation.

missingStatements.text: Elections can be free and fair yet leave citizens unable to change the policies that matter.
missingStatements.rationale: Managed democracy, where governments are legitimated by elections they have learned to control, is the core of Wolin's thesis.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by the new corporate-influence statement and political-elite-corrupt.

missingStatements.text: Corporations have too much influence over government through lobbying and campaign money.
missingStatements.rationale: Wolin and reviewers describe lobbying, contributions and the revolving door as the normal channel of corporate dominance over government.

missingStatements.text: Public services and government functions should not be handed to private companies.
missingStatements.rationale: Wolin sees privatization of public services as the main tool by which corporate power becomes a governing partner.
missingStatements.declined: Privatization of services is not the same as public ownership of major industries (the audit answers public-ownership neutral), and it is a narrow single-audit view.

notes: The thesis is critical and diagnostic; Wolin gives few programmatic remedies beyond local democratic participation, so most positions on unaddressed issues are low-confidence inferences from democratic and anti-corporate principles.
